findings.evidence: <body id="body">; 2 focusable element(s) precede the first heading
findings.violation: The page provides neither a main landmark (a <main> element or role="main") nor a leading same-page skip link.
findings.fix: Add a <main> element wrapping the primary content, or a skip link as the first focusable element linking to it.

findings.violation: The page has no usable title: the title element is missing or empty.
findings.fix: Give the page a specific <title> describing its topic or purpose.

findings.location: line 10, <nav> element, the page's only navigation mechanism
findings.evidence: the nav lists 2 links (Plan a trip, Accessibility); no search form, sitemap link, or breadcrumb trail appears anywhere else in the document
findings.violation: The page exposes only one navigation mechanism, the primary nav menu. WCAG-2.4.5 requires at least two independent mechanisms for a page that is not one step in a linear process, and this rider service updates page is not one.
findings.fix: Add a second independent way to reach this page, such as a site search form, a sitemap link, or a breadcrumb trail, distinct from the primary navigation menu.

findings.evidence: heading text 'Accessibility improvements' is followed by 'Passengers can report a service issue by calling rider services. Updates post to the schedule page within one business day.' and a Zone and Status table (North: On time, South: On time)
findings.violation: The heading 'Accessibility improvements' does not describe the content that follows it. The section covers issue reporting and a zone status table, with no content about accessibility.
findings.fix: Rename the heading to describe its actual content, for example 'Service status' or 'Report an issue', or move genuine accessibility-improvement content under this heading.

findings.violation: The <html> element's lang attribute 'translanguage' is not a well-formed BCP 47 language tag.
findings.fix: Set lang to a well-formed BCP 47 tag identifying the page's default language, for example lang="en".

findings.violation: No text alternative is present and the element is not marked decorative.
findings.fix: Add an alt attribute (or aria-label) describing the image, or mark it decorative with alt="".

findings.violation: Heading level skips from <h2> to <h4> with no intervening level.
findings.fix: Change this heading to <h5>, or add the missing intervening heading level.

findings.violation: The link's accessible name is a generic phrase that gives no clue to its destination out of context.
findings.fix: Rewrite the link text to describe its destination or purpose, or add an aria-label.

findings.evidence: visible text 'Submit', accessible name 'Send form now'
findings.violation: The control's visible text does not appear within its accessible name, so a voice-control user naming the visible label cannot activate it.
findings.fix: Include the visible label text at the start of the aria-label value, or remove the aria-label and rely on the visible text.

findings.evidence: is followed by Enter a 6 character code using letters and numbers only., with no aria-describedby or aria-errormessage on the input referencing the span's id
findings.violation: The invalid promo code field is marked aria-invalid="true" but has no programmatic association to its adjacent error text, so assistive technology exposes that the field is invalid without exposing why.
findings.fix: Add aria-describedby="s3-form-promo-error" to the promo input so its error text is programmatically associated and announced.
